Appreciate the clear ask and the MAP draft. We can definitely run the validation and will include explicit burst vs steady-state testing, queueing behavior analysis, and a TTFT breakdown. High-level proposal below; I'll open a shared MAP doc and sync in the milestones you attached.

Proposed testing plan (summary):
- Week 1 (spike): run burst tests to identify knee points and transient queueing, iterate on rate-limit and autoscale params.
- Week 2 (steady-state): 30m x 3 runs at target sustained RPS to measure token throughput and steady latency percentiles.
- Evaluation: p50/p95/p99 latency, TTFT (time to first token) per request, tokens/sec throughput, error rate, and tail queue depth.

Proposed acceptance criteria (initial):
- Steady p95 latency <= 300 ms (model dependent; we'll calibrate per model variant)
- TTFT <= 500 ms for single-turn inferencing
- Sustained throughput: >= 1,000 tokens/sec for the service tier requested
- Burst tolerance: handle 3x sustained for 60s with graceful degradation (queue depth < 2s equivalent)

I'll loop in Dev to produce a detailed runbook and test harness instructions. Can you confirm the sample traffic and whether you want us to run tests in your VPC (Private) or in our hosted environment?

— Jonas

Folks — following up with a technical plan to drop into the MAP (details for Acme):

Test harness and environment
- We will provide a lightweight harness (Docker + k6 scripts) that can replay sample traffic or run synthetic patterns. Link: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/concurrency-harness (internal)
- Tests will be executed both against Redwood hosted (us-west) and Acme Private (VPC) — run order: hosted spike, hosted steady, private spike, private steady.

Metrics & instrumentation
- Collect per-request: request_id, model_variant, prompt_length, output_tokens, time_to_first_token (ms), time_to_last_token (ms), total_tokens.
- Export traces to our tracing endpoint and push summarized CSVs for the MAP artifacts.

Burst vs steady-state design
- Burst tests: ramp to 3x target RPS over 10s, hold for 60s, then cool down. Repeat 3 times. Measure maximum queue length and error spike.
- Steady-state: 30-minute plateau at target RPS with 5-minute warmup; run 3 repeats across different seeds.

Queueing behavior & rate-limit tuning
- We'll instrument queue depth and latency buckets. If p99 latency rises sharply with minimal queue depth, likely need kernel-level batching tweaks.
- Suggested rate-limit policy for canary: soft limit at target RPS (throttled with 429 + Retry-After), hard limit at 2x target RPS. We will tune to avoid global autoscale churn.

Data artifacts
- Output CSVs (concurrency_test_results_20260711.csv) and a short TL;DR per run.
- We'll also attach a recommended SLO matrix for Acme's tier.

Action owners / timings
- Dev (me): deliver harness and run scripts by Mon 7/13.
- Jonas: coordinate MAP sign-off and scheduling with Acme.
- Camila: prep success criteria for CS acceptance and renewal hooks.

Priya / team — thanks for the CSV and the initial notes. I pulled the attached quick SLO matrix (slo_matrix.png) and did a pass on pragmatic acceptance thresholds based on similar customers running the same model family. Highlights and recommendations: 

Interpretation of early results
- The p99 spike to ~1.2s during burst is consistent with transient queueing when workers hit a batching/kernels knee. Not a hard failure but visible. The ~0.8% error rate likely maps to short TCP resets during the highest pressure window.

Tuning recommendations (what we will change during the spike runs)
1) Batch size cap: lower max_batch for burst windows to reduce TTFT tail while keeping throughput reasonable.
2) KV prefix caching: enable prefix reuse for high-similarity prompts to reduce compute per request.
3) Token packing: run a pass to normalize token lengths (tokenization variance check) — we will add this to the harness.
4) Rate-limit policy: soft-limit at target RPS with 429 + Retry-After and exponential backoff; set hard limit at 2x target RPS for canary.

Proposed acceptance criteria (final, ready for MAP):
- Steady-state p95 latency <= 300 ms
- TTFT p50 <= 180 ms, p95 <= 500 ms
- Sustained throughput >= 1,200 tokens/sec (model: open-7b-quantized)
- Burst handling: tolerate 3x sustained for 60s with p95 degradation < 2x baseline and error rate < 1.5%
- No data-plane regressions between hosted and private beyond 10% throughput variance

Next steps and timeline
- Mon 7/13: Dev delivers harness + instructions; Acme provides continuous weekend traffic if desired.
- Tue 7/14: Redwood runs hosted spike/steady runs and uploads CSVs.
- Thu 7/16: Private runs (if needed) and final SLO matrix updated.
- Tue 7/20: Canary rollout in a controlled lane; procurement sign-off gate.

Please sign off on these acceptance criteria or flag any changes by EOD Mon 7/13 so we can lock the MAP.

Best,
